newsitem.title: THAILAND: Support from monk a hot item in Thai election.
newsitem.headline: Support from monk a hot item in Thai election.

text.p: Political parties in northeastern Thailand are wrangling over who has the backing of a revered Buddhist monk in Sunday's general election.
Opposing parties are trying to woo supporters by playing tapes of Luang Poh (father) Khoon Parisuto -- and each claims it has been granted his support.
Luang Poh Khoon is the popular abbot of a temple in Nakhorn Ratchasima northeast of Bangkok, especially among the more superstitious worshippers.
Some believe that if they wear amulets in his likeness they will be protected from danger.
Party candidates are trading accusations that the monk's tapes have been doctored to trick people into thinking one party has the monk's support.

"Our tape is straight-forward, not like the other candidates who have edited and doctored the tape to mislead the public that Luang Poh Khoon supports them," an aide to New Aspiration Party (NAP) candidate Prasert Chanruangthon told Reuters on Wednesday.
The monk said he had not taken sides, but just granted blessings to all who sought them.
"Many candidates exploit my popularity by claiming that I support them despite the fact that I support everyone," he told a television talk show late on Tuesday night.
Most of the candidates in the November 17 election, especially those from hotly contested northeastern constituencies, have visited Luang Poh Khoon at least once to seek his blessing.

A total of 2,310 candidates from 13 political parties are vying for 393 seats in parliament. Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyud's NAP and the Democrat Party of former prime minister Chuan Leekpai are the front runners.
